title: Clue to Father's Vengeance
next_chapter_hook: In the depths of night, as Chen Ji sat cross-legged practicing Tuna Breathing, a faint, barely perceptible sound of something piercing through the air drifted past the window—someone was probing his dwelling.

text.content: Ling Yuan's gaze was like an ancient deep well, lingering on Chen Ji for three breaths. The surrounding Servant Disciples had long been silenced, afraid that even a glance from the old sect master's residual gaze might fall upon them. Yet Chen Ji only lowered his head, clutching the broom, shoulders slightly hunched—every inch the spineless废物模样. But only he knew that during those three breaths, a thin layer of cold sweat had already formed on the back of his neck—Ling Yuan's gaze was far too unusual. It was not the indifferent look one gives a废物, but rather the cold assessment of a hunter studying its prey. What was he evaluating? Chen Ji pressed this question into the depths of his heart, yet his surface demeanor became even more humbly bowed.

Only when Ling Yuan's figure disappeared at the end of the Mountain Path did Chen Ji slowly straighten his back, a flash of cold killing intent flickering in his eyes. Three days. Since that 'chance encounter' with Ling Yuan at the edge of the Forbidden Grounds, the old sect master's gaze at him had changed. From initial indifference to a certain obscure scrutiny. Chen Ji gripped the broom tighter, his mind ringing with alarm. The waters of the Tianqing Sect ran deeper than he had imagined. What mattered most now was to quickly investigate the cause of his father's death—he had an intuition that Ling Yuan's诡异 gaze might somehow be connected to that 'accident' three years ago.

dialogue.content: Father... what did you discover three years ago to invite such a death?

text.content: Night fell. Most of the lights in the Scripture Repository had already dimmed, and the patrolling stewards had just completed a round. Chen Ji, like a soundless shadow, slipped through the gap of a rear window into a corner of the Tianqing Sect's most ancient building. Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, casting mottled shadows among the dust-covered bookshelves. He knew the layout here by heart—over three years, under the pretense of organizing classics, he had memorized the position of every bookshelf, every hidden compartment. Tonight, what he sought was hidden in the most insignificant corner—the Class D registry of Outer Disciples.

As his fingertips brushed across one faded scroll after another, Chen Ji's heartbeat gradually accelerated. The Class D disciple registries were arranged by year, each volume recording Outer Disciples' entry, transfers, promotions, and even... deaths. Chen Dehai. His father. The Outer Disciple/Servant who died of illness three years ago, forty-seven years old. Chen Ji turned to that page, his fingertips trembling slightly. The registry entry was very brief: 'Chen Dehai, in the autumn of Tianqing Year 2987, died of illness at age forty-seven, buried at the sect's western suburban charitable graveyard.' No cause of disease, no detailed explanation, not even a personal signature—only a cursory mark from a scribe who wrote on behalf of others.

Too clean. Clean like a档案 that had been meticulously tampered with. Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, bringing the page closer to the candle flame. In the candlelight, certain characters covered by ink faintly emerged in outline—traces of deliberate scraping and rewriting. His pupils contracted sharply. Flipping to the next page, he saw something even more shocking: his father's entry record had also been tampered with. What should have contained detailed accounts of origin, master, and cultivation level now only showed a blurry ink smear. And at the edge of that ink smear, he faintly made out several remaining characters—'Special... Recommendation...' The characters after were completely illegible.

dialogue.content: Special recommendation... Father, who exactly were you?

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to冷静下来. His pace of flipping through the registry quickened, his fingers like eagle claws rifling through the yellowed pages. More anomalous records emerged—during that period three years ago, at least seven Outer Disciples had vanished from the sect under the name of 'death from illness.' Among them, five people's files, like his father's, had been meticulously falsified. The records of the other two were干脆是一片空白, as if they had never existed. He memorized these names one by one: Chen Dehai, Zhao Si, Zhu Qi, Qian Jiu, Sun Shier... and another name that made his heart tighten sharply—Chen Nian.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian... Nian Nian! These were all people who had contacted Nian Nian three years ago! The time of their 'death from illness' was exactly within three months before and after Nian Nian's disappearance!

text.content: Chen Ji's breathing became rapid. Nian Nian—his sister, that relative who was taken by the Holy sect to become a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'—the truth behind her disappearance three years ago might be hidden within these falsified files. Father, those Outer Disciples, and Nian Nian... what connection existed between them? Why was someone systematically erasing these traces? Just then, a sinister voice suddenly came from behind—'Chen Servant, it's quite late. Servant Disciples are not permitted to wander freely in the Scripture Repository.' Chen Ji猛然回头, only to see a black-robed figure had somehow already stood at the end of the bookshelf, gazing at him with an amused expression.

Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, revealing half of that person's gloomy face—it was the night duty steward of the Scripture Repository, Qian Dewang. This person's cultivation was not high, only Qi Refining Seventh Stage, but because he was responsible for managing the classics, he had mastered quite a bit of disciples' file information. More importantly, this person had always been extremely close with certain Outer Sect powers, known throughout as a weathercock and informant. At this moment, a meaningful smile hung at the corner of his mouth, his eyes flickering with greedy light—clearly intending to make an article out of tonight's 'chance encounter.'

dialogue.content: Yo, isn't this Chen Servant? Oh, that's not right, should call you Chen Junior Brother. An Outer Disciple/Servant like you, coming to the Scripture Repository in the middle of the night to read what books? Could it be you're looking into something... unspeakable?

choice.prompt: Qian Dewang's appearance made the situation suddenly tense; Chen Ji had to make a choice:

choices.description: Play the innocent废物, using a humble posture to defuse the crisis—'Brother Qian misunderstood, your junior brother only dropped something here while sweeping during the day, came specially to look for it...'
choices.visible_cost: Abandon the opportunity to investigate leads
choices.risk_hint: Qian Dewang might not believe it and will continue to harass

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze instantly became vacant and helpless, his shoulders shrinking, perfectly embodying the panicked appearance of someone caught with damaging evidence. 'Qian, Qian Brother...' he stammered, 'your junior brother dropped my mother's Jade Pendant here while sweeping during the day. This is her临终遗物啊... I beg Brother to be merciful, your junior brother will find it and leave immediately, absolutely no daring to touch sect classics!' As he spoke, his eye rims actually reddened slightly, his acting refined enough to fool anyone.

dialogue.content: Qian Dewang narrowed his eyes, clearly not believing this explanation. He leisurely walked closer a few steps, his gaze sweeping over the registry in Chen Ji's hands—but Chen Ji had flipped past that crucial record the instant he began speaking, now holding only an unimportant 'Illustrated Guide to Spiritual Herbs.'

choices.description: Use leverage to counterattack, making Qian Dewang投鼠忌器—This person is a known weathercock, as long as you let him know you're not easy to mess with, he'll naturally weigh the pros and cons
choices.visible_cost: Expose that he is not a一无所知的废物
choices.visible_reward: Intimidate Qian Dewang, gain breathing room
choices.risk_hint: May alert the forces behind Qian Dewang

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze transformed numerous times in that split second. Cowardice, panic, fear—these carefully constructed masks were收敛干净 in an instant, replaced by an ice-cold intensity. Qian Dewang's smile froze on his face, because he suddenly discovered that this废物 Servant had transformed completely in an instant. There was no panic in those eyes at all; instead, they reflected something that made his spine go cold.

dialogue.content: Steward Qian,' Chen Ji's voice was low and calm, 'patrolling alone in the Scripture Repository at night, and specifically coming to the Outer Disciple registry area—could it be you're also looking for something? Or... are you watching someone on behalf of someone?'

choices.description: Qian Dewang is notoriously greedy; as long as the benefits are sufficient, he will反而成为自己的棋子—'Brother Qian, this is a Qi Gathering Elixir, why must brothers make things difficult for each other?'
choices.visible_cost: Lose one precious Qi Gathering Elixir
choices.visible_reward: Bribe Qian Dewang, gain an intelligence source
choices.risk_hint: This person is a weathercock and may be outbid by higher offers

text.content: A harmless smile slowly formed at the corner of Chen Ji's lips. He slowly took out a jade bottle from his怀, swaying it in the moonlight. 'Brother Qian,辛苦了 patrolling at night. This Qi Gathering Elixir is what your junior brother obtained through fortune; I was just looking for an opportunity to offer it to Brother...' Qian Dewang's eyes immediately lit up, but then restored some vigilance—where did this废物 get an elixir?

dialogue.content: Brother can rest assured,' Chen Ji lowered his voice, 'your junior brother only wants to investigate some old matters about my father, definitely will not implicate Brother. As for the origin of this elixir... Brother has no need to know, right? We're all smart people, why push things to extremes?'

text.content: Qian Dewang stared at Chen Ji for a full ten breaths, his expression fluctuating unceasingly. He clearly hadn't expected this lowly废物 Servant who was always submissive to be so difficult tonight. That speech was watertight, neither admitting nor denying, yet clearly implying—Qian Dewang's presence here at night was equally untenable. After a stalemate for a moment, Qian Dewang dryly laughed and proactively stepped back. 'Junior Brother Chen jests; Brother was merely conducting routine patrols.' His tone softened, but the gloom in his eyes deepened, 'However, some things, Junior Brother better not investigate too deeply. The old archives in this Scripture Repository... involve things much bigger than you imagine.'

dialogue.content: Some dead people should just let them rest in peace. If the living meddle too much... Heh, Brother means well, simply reminding Junior Brother.

text.content: After speaking these meaningful words, Qian Dewang turned and left, his footsteps gradually fading down the corridor. The Scripture Repository sank back into deathly silence, only the night wind outside the windows mournfully passing through the eaves. Chen Ji stood alone, his brow tightly knit. Qian Dewang's warning was绝非空穴来风—'things bigger than you imagine,' the weight of these words he understood clearly. Father's identity, those 'death from illness' disciples three years ago, and Nian Nian's disappearance... behind all this, what kind of behemoth was hidden? What alarmed him more was Qian Dewang's gaze as he left—not retreat after being intimidated, but rather... a waiting.

choice.prompt: Qian Dewang had already left, but Chen Ji knew tonight would not end here. Now he needed to decide his next move:

choices.description: Seize the opportunity while Qian Dewang was away, continue flipping through files, find more clues—even at the risk of being discovered
choices.risk_hint: Qian Dewang may go to report

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate long. Qian Dewang's departure itself was a signal—either going for reinforcements, or going to report. Either way, his time was running out. He quickly flipped through files, memorizing those falsified records one by one. Meanwhile, he noticed a detail: on the back cover of Chen Dehai's file, there was a line of extremely faint ink, barely visible unless carefully looked for. It was a coordinate—the sect's western suburb, near the charitable graveyard, the location of an old locust tree.

Father left this! Chen Ji's heart lurched. He forced himself to suppress the excitement, quickly returned the registry to its place, then climbed out through the rear window. Night was as ink, shrouding the连绵屋脊 of the Tianqing Sect. He must leave the Scripture Repository area quickly—but simultaneously, a bold plan was already forming in his mind. Western suburban graveyard, Father's tomb... perhaps there lay the key to this entire matter.

choices.description: Tonight's gains are sufficient enough, should not continue taking risks—first digest existing clues, come another day
choices.risk_hint: Files may be destroyed in advance

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and made the more prudent choice. Tonight's information volume was already enormous—Father's anomalous file, those 'death from illness' disciples three years ago, and the connection to Nian Nian's disappearance... he needed time to digest these clues,更需要时间布局下一步. Rather than taking risks in such an environment, better to retreat and plan from长计议. He quietly left through the rear window, his figure dissolving into the night.

However, the instant he climbed out the window, an uncanny sensation suddenly washed over him—something, as if, was watching him from within the darkness. He猛然回头, only seeing the empty window lattice and flickering candlelight. An illusion? Chen Ji dared not be careless,quickening his pace and disappearing into the night. And shortly after he left, in the shadows of the Scripture Repository's third floor, a pair of eyes slowly opened, staring in the direction he had vanished...

Returning to his dilapidated woodshed, Chen Ji tightly closed the doors and windows, sitting cross-legged on the简陋 wooden bed. Moonlight leaked through the window seams, casting a pallid white strip of light on the ground. He closed his eyes, rapidly sorting through the information obtained tonight. Father's identity was far from simple on the surface—those four characters 'Special Recommendation' meant his entry into the Tianqing Sect had been deliberately arranged by someone. And those 'death from illness' disciples three years ago, together with Nian Nian's disappearance... all this pointed to a possibility: someone was executing some kind of plan, and Father and Nian Nian might both be... insiders or even participants in this plan.

dialogue.content: (Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, carrying a hint of赞许) Well done, child. You are more cautious than I anticipated. Tonight you have touched upon something certain people do not want touched... but it's not enough, far from enough.
Mo Xiansheng, that coordinate Father left behind...

(Mo Xiansheng沉默了片刻, his voice becoming grave) Western suburban graveyard... what is buried there is not just bones, but also what your father traded his life for. But not tonight. You have been noticed—that Qian Dewang is merely a dog; the true master is still in the shadows. Going to the graveyard rashly will only see you follow your father's footsteps.

text.content: Chen Ji tightly clenched his fist, his knuckles whitening from the force. He raised his head, his gaze falling upon that pallid moon outside the window, burning with suppressed fury. 'Father...' his voice was soft yet carried an unquestionable determination, 'rest assured. No matter who those people are, no matter how great their power... I will dig them out one by one. The suffering you and Nian Nian endured, I will make them repay a hundredfold.' The moment his words fell, a faint sound of something piercing through the air suddenly passed outside the window—that was a sound only a高手 of extremely superb轻功 could produce. Chen Ji's expression instantly cooled. Here they come. The people behind Qian Dewang, truly did not let him off.

He did not move, only slowed his breathing, maintaining the posture of cross-legged Tuna Breathing. In his perception, a faint yet tangible presence was lingering outside his woodshed, seemingly probing. That presence's cultivation was not low, at least Qi Refining Ninth Stage and above, nothing like a character such as Qian Dewang. The corner of Chen Ji's lips slightly lifted, revealing a cold, fierce arc. Sending people to probe? Then let them try. He secretly gripped the Tianji Record Fragment in his palm, but did not activate it—not worth wasting Heavenly Fate Value on such small fry. The visitor meant no good, but tonight, he still did not want to reveal too many底牌. The movement outside continued for about一刻钟, finally gradually fading away. Only then did Chen Ji slowly open his eyes, his gaze deep and profound as an abyss.

Someone was searching his residence. The moment that presence completely vanished, Chen Ji immediately rose and began checking every corner of the room. His movements were swift, light, yet carried a凌厉 quality completely at odds with his outward appearance. Floor,墙角, under the bed—he examined them one by one, and soon discovered several traces of disturbance. Someone had rifled through his things. The force of the search was not too great, clearly the other party only wanted to confirm the existence of certain items, rather than necessarily finding them. Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted. 'Looking for the Tianji Record?' he murmured to himself, 'Or perhaps... looking for what Father left behind?' Either way meant that the disturbance at the Scripture Repository tonight had already alerted certain people who should not have been alerted.

dialogue.content: Good.' Chen Ji said softly, his tone actually carrying a hint of a smile, 'Since you're so eager to jump out, then don't blame me for dragging you out one by one. Father's death, Nian Nian's disappearance... and all you rats hiding in the dark, I have plenty of patience to play this game with you.

text.content: He lay back on the bed again, yet kept his eyes open, staring at the ceiling
